name: minimal
label: Minimal
description: Fades only, and short ones. Nothing slides, nothing scales, nothing sweeps: a window appears and disappears by opacity alone over 90 ms, a layer fades in over 120 ms, and the focus border still changes colour in 90 ms so focus stays visible. This is the preset reduce-motion resolves to, and it is the accessibility floor of the motion system — the least motion that still tells a person what changed.
source: Hyprland v0.57.2, read out into data/design/animations.json: leaf names and their parents from src/config/shared/animation/AnimationTree.cpp, the per-leaf style lists from AnimationManager::styleValidInConfigVar, and the numeric bounds from src/config/lua/bindings/LuaBindingsConfigRules.cpp with src/config/lua/types/LuaConfigFloat.cpp — bezier components in [-1, 2], spring values strictly above 0.5, speed in (0, 100] where duration_ms = 100 * speed, every one of them a config error rather than a clamp.

windows._note: Disabled, not merely given a fade: the window leaves only accept slide, gnome, gnomed and popin — there is no fade style for them — so 'fades only' means the transform is off and the opacity fade below does the work. Window opacity is a sibling branch of the tree (fade's parent is global, windows' parent is global), so turning windows off leaves fadeIn and fadeOut animating.

workspaces._note: A workspace switch becomes an instant cut. slidevert and fade are the alternatives this leaf accepts, but a full-screen slide is the single largest motion on the desktop and the one reduce-motion exists to remove; the fade style here would cross-fade two workspaces, which costs a full-screen composite per frame for no clarity.

borderangle._note: The looping gradient sweep is off. It is continuous per-frame compositor work that reports no interaction, which makes it the first thing to remove in a minimal or reduce-motion mode and a real part of what game mode gains.

border._note: Kept, and kept short. The focus border is how a person knows which window has the keyboard, so removing it would trade a motion problem for an orientation problem; 90 ms is a colour change that reads as immediate.

_note: No curve in this file overshoots and no spring is declared: every component is inside the [0, 1] unit square, so this preset would also be renderable as CSS if a toolkit surface ever needed the same feel. Enabled durations are 90 or 120 ms, and reduce-motion caps them at tokens.json motion.animation.reduce_motion.max_duration_ms (90), which is what brings the two 120 ms layer fades down to the ceiling -- the cap exists for every preset, and minimal is close enough to it that turning reduce-motion on barely changes anything. Seven events are disabled with an explicit enabled = false rather than being left out of the file: an absent leaf keeps inheriting its parent's animation (windowsIn from windows, specialWorkspace from workspaces), so omitting an entry would not turn anything off. hl.animation returns early on enabled = false after setConfigForNode(leaf, false, 1, "default"), which is why a disabled event carries no duration, curve or style.
